Sewerage and Drainage System:
HUD agrees that it is important to state that a water conservation program would further help to decrease incremental excremental flow.
Regarding industrial wastewater flows not being revealed in the report, there was presented estimated sewage flows which included an estimate of the industrial flow. The industrial component which went into this was 0.7 mgd for the Preferred Plan which represents 75 percent of the flow. That the final report should expand the scope of water and sewerage system to include industrial water usage and discharge is not necessary since that has already been done.
Regarding the drainage system, page 34, Part I of the report identifies the construction of utility and transportation improvements as among the earliest activities of the program.
Solid Waste:
While the comments of the EOEA on solid waste generally are more applicable to a later design phase of the project, we can state that the Authority will encourage, to the extent feasible, the establishment of a comprehensive solid waste management program as well as the participation of users in the waste recycling program.
Water and Energy Conservation:
For some time the Authority has been discussing with State and Federal officials a proposal to establish an energy resources and conservation system to service new, mixed-use, multiple-building development in Kendall Square. Those discussions are continuing. Concomitantly, the Authority has made it clear to all potential developers that it expects, at a minimum, that a major effort be made to conserve energy in building and interbuilding development and operations. The Authority will also encourage, to the extent feasible, maximum water conservation measures.
Construction Phases
The Authority will take all appropriate and necessary measures to prevent and/or minimize adverse environmental impacts resulting from construction phase activities.
